title: Linear conditional-information bounds for VC learning
formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(c>0\) such that the following holds? For every nonempty Boolean hypothesis class \(H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}\) of finite VC dimension \(d\ge1\), and every integer \(n\ge d\), there is a proper randomized learner \(A:(X\times\{0,1\})^n\to H\) satisfying both \[\forall P,\quad \operatorname{CMI}_{P}(A)\le cd\] and \[\forall s\in(X\times\{0,1\})^n,\quad \mathbb E_{W\sim A(s)}\widehat L_s(W)\le\inf_{h\in H}\widehat L_s(h)+c\sqrt{d/n}?\] The first quantifier ranges over all labeled-data distributions in the measurable model below, including nonrealizable distributions. The second ranges over every deterministic sample, including samples with conflicting labels. The same learner must satisfy both guarantees; it may depend on \(H,n\), but not on \(P\). This is the original source’s main agnostic Conjecture 6, recovered from the imported introduction excerpt, not its different realizable or improper variants.

source_formulation.text: For every VC class, does there exist a proper learner with conditional mutual information linear in VC dimension and expected empirical loss within a universal constant times the square root of dimension divided by sample size of the best empirical loss?
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase

why: Classical VC theory controls prediction error through the richness of a class. This question asks whether the same optimal scale can always be realized by a learner whose whole output reveals only a dimension-proportional amount about which examples were used. The joint information and empirical-accuracy requirements make it a statement about the learner itself.
status_note: Historical source: Steinke–Zakynthinou 2020 Conjecture 6, the proper agnostic statement. The known November 2020 negative theorem concerns Conjectures 7–8 with smaller realizable empirical error, and the checked 2021/2025 information analyses do not themselves match Conjecture 6. Crucially, the official FOCS 2026 accepted list and Hanneke’s author page list “The optimal information complexity of VC learning” by Hanneke and Juexiao Wang. No theorem text or manuscript link was located in the bounded checks on 16 September 2026. Current status is therefore uncertain, with that specific comparison outstanding; this review does not assert that the conjecture remains open.

category_assignment.reason: The desired construction is a VC learner with optimal information usage, rather than a distributed protocol.

importance.reason: A central comparison between VC learning and information-based generalization, asking whether the logarithmic sample-size overhead can be removed for proper agnostic learners. The full-output and pointwise-accuracy requirements distinguish it from already optimal prediction-error analyses.

sentences: The card asks whether every finite-VC binary class has a proper learner whose whole output has conditional information only linear in the dimension.
The same learner must achieve expected training error within a universal square-root dimension-to-sample-size term of the best hypothesis on every sample.
The information experiment reveals two candidates per training position and measures what the output says about the hidden choices.
Known negative results concern stricter realizable training guarantees, while other optimal generalization analyses use different information bounds.
A directly relevant FOCS 2026 paper is accepted but its theorem text was not located, so the completed formulation retains uncertain current status.

definitions:
A hypothesis is a total function \(h:X\to\{0,1\}\). A finite set \(V\subseteq X\) is shattered if every map \(V\to\{0,1\}\) is the restriction of a hypothesis in \(H\); the VC dimension is the supremum of sizes of shattered finite sets. For a labeled sequence \(s=((x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^n\), its empirical zero-one loss is \(\widehat L_s(h)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{h(x_i)\ne y_i\}\). Samples are ordered and may contain repeated points. Proper means that every output is a member of \(H\), rather than an arbitrary Boolean predictor. The expected empirical loss averages only the learner’s private randomness, with the input sequence held fixed. There is no running-time, finite encoding, efficient evaluation, or finite/countable-domain restriction.

The following explicit measurable-kernel convention makes the source’s probability notation meaningful. Equip \(X\) and the hypothesis space \(H\) with sigma-algebras for which evaluation \((h,x)\mapsto h(x)\) is jointly measurable; binary labels have all subsets. The statement quantifies over such measurable presentations of the classes. A randomized learner is a probability kernel from the product sample space into \(H\): for each input it assigns a probability distribution on \(H\), and probabilities of measurable output events vary measurably with the input. Deterministic learners are included. All distributions \(P\) on the labeled product space are allowed. This is a stated probability-interface convention, not a finite-domain specialization, a premise that a measurable empirical-risk minimizer exists, or a claim about nonmeasurable learning rules. It should be retained explicitly in a formalization.

For \(\operatorname{CMI}_{P}(A)\), draw a supersample \(\widetilde Z=(Z_{i,b})_{1\le i\le n,\ b\in\{0,1\}}\) of \(2n\) independent labeled examples from \(P\), and independently draw a uniformly random selector \(B\in\{0,1\}^n\). Let \(\widetilde Z_B=(Z_{i,B_i})_{i=1}^n\), then draw \(W\) from the kernel \(A(\widetilde Z_B)\) using no access to the unselected examples. Define \[\operatorname{CMI}_{P}(A)=I(W;B\mid\widetilde Z)=n-H(B\mid W,\widetilde Z)\] in bits. Here \(H(B\mid W,\widetilde Z)=\mathbb E[-\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}^n}p_b\log_2 p_b]\), where \(p_b=\mathbb E[\mathbf1\{B=b\}\mid\sigma(W,\widetilde Z)]\), and \(0\log_2 0=0\). This finite-selector definition uses conditional expectation and does not need pointwise conditional densities on arbitrary domains. The quantity lies between zero and \(n\). It measures the complete hypothesis-valued output \(W\) under its stated measurable structure, not merely the labels it predicts on the supersample and not the learner’s unreleased random seed. Changing logarithm base only rescales the universal constant. The learner cannot see \(P\), the supersample or selector as additional inputs. The accuracy slack and information constant are uniform over all classes, dimensions and sample sizes; a bound with an extra \(\log n\), or with a class-dependent constant, is a different assertion.
answer_criterion: Give a Lean-checked proof of Conjecture 6 in the explicitly stated probability convention, or prove its logical negation. A positive answer supplies one universal \(c\) and a proper probability kernel for every admitted \(H,n\), with the distribution-uniform CMI bound and pointwise empirical-loss bound both established. A negative answer must show that for every proposed \(c>0\), some admitted class and sample size defeat every proper kernel: either some distribution violates the information bound, or some deterministic sample violates the expected empirical-loss bound. A counterexample only to exact consistency or to empirical loss \(O(d/n)\) does not refute the allowed \(O(\sqrt{d/n})\) slack here. A generalization bound using a different information quantity, an improper output, or a distribution-dependent learner does not prove this claim. The target is existence with universal constants, not a numerical quantity requiring additive approximation.

context_blocks.text: Conditional mutual information exposes two candidates for each training position and measures what the final hypothesis reveals about which candidate was selected. Conditioning on both candidates avoids the unbounded information cost that can arise when an algorithm reveals a real-valued observation under ordinary mutual information.

The source’s Theorem 5 gives an empirical-risk minimizer with conditional information at most \(d\log n+2\), in its logarithm convention. Empirical-risk minimization chooses a hypothesis with the fewest training errors. Conjecture 6 permits a controlled excess in this empirical error while asking that the extra sample-size dependence disappear from the information bound.

The source also states Conjectures 7 and 8 for realizable samples. They demand expected empirical loss \(O(d/n)\), or zero, together with the linear information bound. Haghifam and coauthors’ Theorem 4.2 refutes those two proper-learning claims, even if the information bound is replaced by an arbitrary dimension-only function. Its smaller empirical-loss allowance is essential; that theorem does not supply a refutation of Conjecture 6 as displayed here.

The same lower-bound paper notes that chaining conditional-information analyses yields the optimal \(O(\sqrt{d/n})\) expected generalization scale. That fact concerns the resulting bound on prediction behavior. It does not assert that a single learner’s complete output has CMI at most \(cd\) while satisfying the present pointwise training guarantee.

The 2021 PAC-Bayes/CMI paper’s VC-class Theorem 13 retains an information term \(d\log(2n)\). This extends information-based generalization guarantees, but it does not remove the sample-size dependence required to answer Conjecture 6.

The 2025 projection paper controls an auxiliary compressed real-vector output and a distortion term. Its checked theorem does not state the present universal proper binary learning claim with dimension-only information about the complete output and a pointwise training guarantee.

The official FOCS 2026 list now includes Hanneke and Wang’s “The optimal information complexity of VC learning.” The author’s publication page confirms the entry, but the checked entries supply no manuscript or theorem statement. This is a concrete unresolved status lead: the title alone does not establish whether the proper agnostic Conjecture 6, a realizable variant, or another information model has been settled. The card therefore retains uncertain status rather than asserting current openness or a resolution.
